title: China gold market update: Robust demand in October
gist: World Gold Council's October 2026 China update: gold fell ~6% in USD and RMB to new 2026 lows, yet Chinese ETFs hit a record 310t, SGE withdrawals rose unseasonally and the PBoC bought 26t, its biggest monthly purchase since October 2023. WGC frames a structural shift where bar/coin investment has overtaken jewellery as the driver of Chinese wholesale demand, while equity stabilisation threatens ETF flows.

themes.theme: October gold sell-off and RMB effect

insights.claim: The LBMA Gold Price PM in USD fell 6.3% and the Shanghai Benchmark Gold Price PM (SHAUPM) in RMB fell 5.9% in October 2026, extending September's weakness.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Two consecutive monthly declines signal momentum has turned against gold; watch for capitulation vs dip-buying.

insights.claim: World Gold Council attributes gold's October 2026 weakness mainly to a rotation of funds out of equities and gold futures into bonds, with heavier selling in US trading via COMEX futures and US gold ETFs.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Bond-rally-driven rotation is a gold headwind; track US ETF flows and COMEX positioning as the marginal seller.
insights.quote: A rotation of funds out of equities and gold futures into bonds could be a key driver of gold’s weakness during the month.

insights.claim: By end-October 2026 gold was down 7.1% year-to-date in USD and 9.4% in RMB, with sharp RMB appreciation against the dollar explaining the deeper loss for Chinese holders.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: RMB strength erodes local-currency gold returns, a drag on Chinese investor appetite if it persists.

insights.claim: The LBMA Gold Price PM closed at US$3,870/oz around 16 November 2026, the lowest daily close of 2026, after a short-lived early-November rebound following the US mid-terms.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Gold is making new YTD lows; key level to watch for further downside or base-building.

insights.claim: World Gold Council expects shifting expectations of the Fed's policy path in response to data releases to drive near-term gold sentiment, while the impact of the US mid-term results remains uncertain.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Gold trades as a Fed-expectations instrument near term; macro data surprises are the catalyst.
insights.locator: Gold began to rebound in early November

themes.theme: Chinese gold ETFs: record tonnage, fading momentum

insights.claim: Chinese gold ETFs added 6.3t (RMB5.3bn, US$784mn) in October 2026, a fourth consecutive monthly inflow, lifting holdings to a month-end record of 310t with 62t added year-to-date.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Chinese ETF demand is a structural bid even into falling prices.
insights.locator: Chinese gold ETFs have seen inflows four months in a row

insights.claim: Chinese gold ETF AUM fell 4% to RMB265bn (US$40bn) in October 2026 despite tonnage inflows, because the lower gold price more than offset the inflow.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: AUM declines mask continued tonnage accumulation; use tonnes, not value, to read demand.
insights.locator: Chinese gold ETFs have seen inflows four months in a row

insights.claim: Chinese investors' allocation to gold ETFs has been driven by equity market weakness, low government bond yields and the PBoC's continuous gold-purchase announcements.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A sustained Chinese equity recovery or rising CGB yields would remove key supports for Chinese gold ETF demand.

insights.claim: Chinese gold ETFs swung to modest outflows in early November 2026 as Beijing's measures to stabilise the stock market diverted local investor interest away from gold and falling prices deterred buyers.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Chinese equity stabilisation competes directly with gold for local flows; watch policy support for A-shares.
insights.locator: In early November gold ETFs reversed

insights.claim: Average daily gold futures trading volume on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) fell 28% m/m to 258t/day in October 2026.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Cooling speculative activity in China reduces a source of price momentum.

insights.claim: Net longs held by the top 20 SHFE gold futures participants fell 15t from end-September to 134t in October 2026, though they remained 31% higher year-on-year.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Speculative length is being trimmed but still elevated y/y, leaving room for further liquidation.

themes.theme: Investment replacing jewellery in wholesale demand

insights.claim: Gold withdrawals from the Shanghai Gold Exchange (SGE) rose an unseasonal 2% m/m to 94t in October 2026, driven by dip-buying in bullion and jeweller restocking after National Day Holiday sales, though still 24% lower y/y.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Physical dip-buying in China provides support beneath price weakness.
insights.locator: Another October of unseasonal wholesale demand strength

insights.claim: World Gold Council argues China's wholesale gold market is undergoing a structural shift in which investment demand is replacing jewellery consumption as the key driver of SGE withdrawals, beginning in 2025 and strengthening in 2026.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Traditional jewellery-based seasonal models for Chinese demand are becoming unreliable; model bar/coin demand instead.
insights.quote: In our view, this reflects a broader shift in China’s wholesale gold market, with investment demand increasingly replacing jewellery consumption as the key driver of withdrawals.
insights.locator: Another October of unseasonal wholesale demand strength

insights.claim: Chinese bar and coin investment exceeded jewellery consumption for the first time in history in 2025, and the same holds so far in 2026, driven by cautious discretionary spending, value-preservation demand and the late-2025 VAT reform that benefited bullion buying.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: China's gold demand is now more price-insensitive investment demand than discretionary jewellery buying.
insights.quote: Bar and coin investment in 2025 notably exceeded jewellery consumption for the first time in history
insights.locator: Another October of unseasonal wholesale demand strength

insights.claim: The People's Bank of China (PBoC) reported a 26t gold addition in October 2026, its largest monthly purchase since October 2023 and the 24th consecutive month of buying, taking official holdings to 2,435t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The PBoC is a price-insensitive buyer that accelerates on dips, providing an official-sector floor.
insights.locator: The PBoC reported larger gold buying

insights.claim: Gold's share of China's FX reserves fell to 8.1% in October 2026 from 8.5% in September because the value of PBoC gold reserves contracted 5.3% on lower prices despite the tonnage addition.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Low gold share of reserves leaves ample room for further PBoC accumulation.
insights.locator: The PBoC reported larger gold buying

insights.claim: PBoC gold purchase announcements are cited by World Gold Council as a confidence anchor that encourages Chinese retail and ETF investors to buy gold.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: PBoC monthly reserve data doubles as a signal driving Chinese private demand; a pause would be a sentiment risk.

insights.claim: China's net gold imports rose to 129t in September 2026, 5t higher than August and up 41% y/y, supported by pre-peak-season wholesale demand and a rising local gold price premium.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Rising Chinese imports and local premium indicate tight onshore physical demand.
insights.locator: Gold imports rose further in September

insights.claim: World Gold Council expects Chinese bullion investment to stay supported by the macro backdrop and jewellery consumption to improve on seasonality and lower prices, but warns a persistent equity market recovery could divert attention from gold ETFs.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Base case is steady Chinese physical demand; the key downside risk is an equity rally pulling ETF flows.
